factual_errors.claim: Step 1-2 recommend re-checking baud rate/parity/slave ID and wiring/termination as likely causes.
factual_errors.why_wrong: The question states that ModScan can successfully poll the same registers when the gateway loses communication. A working master on the same physical link rules out a wiring/termination/electrical-settings mismatch as the cause -- if those were wrong, ModScan would fail too. Recommending a full physical-layer recheck ignores this constraint in the question and misdirects diagnostic effort away from gateway-side causes (session/connection limits, idle-timeout handling) that would actually explain a persistent client succeeding while the gateway intermittently fails.

notes: The answer never asserts a specific wrong technical fact the way the AUMA answer does -- it stays at the level of plausible-sounding generic troubleshooting (settings match, wiring, timeout/retry values, protocol analyzer capture, swap-test with another master) and ends with a genuinely useful diagnostic question about timeout vs. illegal-function errors in the log. But it misses the actual diagnostic insight this scenario points to: ModScan opening its own persistent connection succeeding while a gateway with a small simultaneous-connection ceiling intermittently fails is a textbook connection-pool-exhaustion / idle-timeout signature, and the answer doesn't mention connection limits or idle timeouts at all. It also doesn't use the ModScan-success clue to rule out the physical-layer checks it recommends first. Reasonable diagnostic hygiene, but incomplete and not ranked by likelihood.
